plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down. Bidding above value risks winning and overpaying relative to value; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $30, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $30, ensuring I only win when profitable and pay a fair second-price amount.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids. My value is $1, which is very low. Bidding above my value risks losing money if I win at a price above $1; bidding below risks losing a profitable opportunity. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. I'll bid exactly $1.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $40 to maximize expected profit.
